title: Shakshuka
subtitle: Eggs poached in spiced tomato and pepper sauce
excerpt: Eggs cracked directly into a spiced, garlicky tomato and pepper sauce and cooked until the whites are just set and the yolks still runny. Served in the pan with warm flatbread. A beloved Levantine breakfast.

recipe.sourceNotes: Shakshuka is a dish of eggs poached in a spiced tomato sauce, eaten widely across North Africa and the Levant. It is particularly associated with Israeli, Tunisian, Libyan, and Egyptian cooking. The name likely derives from the Maghrebi Arabic for 'mixture'. It became popular in Britain as a brunch dish from the 2010s onwards, appearing on café menus across the country. The sauce base is versatile and works with many additions: spinach, chickpeas, feta, or merguez sausage.

recipeTools.notes: With a lid, or cover with foil.

content.text: Make wells in the sauce before cracking the eggs in: this stops them spreading. Cover the pan after adding the eggs to trap steam and help the whites set without over-cooking the yolks. Check frequently towards the end: the yolks should be runny when the pan comes off the heat, as they continue to cook in the residual heat.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Fry the onion and pepper for 8 minutes until softened. Add the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, and chilli flakes. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the tinned tomatoes. Season with salt. Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce has thickened slightly.
Make 6 wells in the sauce. Crack an egg into each well. Cover the pan with a lid or foil. Cook over low heat for 5 to 7 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks are still runny.
Scatter with coriander and crumbled feta if using. Serve directly from the pan with flatbread or crusty bread.
